---
title: "Benchmarking Goals and Context"
---

Before diving into benchmarking, consider what you want to learn. Your goals
determine which criterium features and analysis methods are most appropriate.

## What is your goal in benchmarking?

Common benchmarking goals include:

- **Performance validation**: Verify code meets latency requirements
- **Regression detection**: Catch performance degradations
- **Implementation comparison**: Choose between alternative approaches
- **Optimization guidance**: Identify where optimization effort pays off
- **Capacity planning**: Understand throughput limits

## Is this code on a hotpath?

Code executed frequently (hotpaths) receives aggressive JIT optimization.
Infrequently executed code may never be fully optimized.

| Execution Pattern | Warmup Approach | See |
|-------------------|-----------------|-----|
| Hotpath (called millions of times) | Full JIT warmup with varied inputs | [Warmup](./criterium.warmup_notebook.html) |
| Occasional (called periodically) | Reduced warmup, measure cold performance | [Basic Usage](./criterium.basic_usage_notebook.html) |
| One-shot (startup, initialization) | Minimal warmup, focus on first-call time | [Bench Options](./criterium.bench_options_notebook.html) |

## What is the normal calling pattern?

The JIT optimizes based on observed inputs. Warmup should use representative
arguments to avoid over-specialization.

**Questions to consider:**

- What argument sizes occur in production?
- Is there variation in input characteristics?
- Are there multiple calling contexts?

Use `:warmup-args-fn` to provide varied inputs during warmup. See
[Warmup](./criterium.warmup_notebook.html) and
[Argument Generation](./criterium.arg_gen_notebook.html) for techniques.

## In-place or isolated measurement?

| Approach | Use When | See |
|----------|----------|-----|
| **Isolated** (standalone bench) | Measuring algorithm performance independent of system | [Basic Usage](./criterium.basic_usage_notebook.html) |
| **In-place** (instrumented) | Understanding performance in production context | [Instrumented Functions](./criterium.instrument_fn_notebook.html) |
| **Sampled** (periodic capture) | Long-running systems with minimal overhead | [Sampled Functions](./criterium.sampled_fn_notebook.html) |

## Typical or unusual performance?

| Interest | Analysis Method | See |
|----------|-----------------|-----|
| **Typical** (mean, median) | Standard statistics | [Basic Usage](./criterium.basic_usage_notebook.html) |
| **Distribution shape** | KDE, histogram | [KDE Analysis](./criterium.kde_analysis_notebook.html) |
| **Worst-case latency** | Tail analysis, percentiles | [Tail Analysis](./criterium.tail_analysis_notebook.html) |
| **Fitting models** | Distribution fitting | [Distribution Fitting](./criterium.distribution_fitting_notebook.html) |

## Single point or range of inputs?

| Scope | Approach | See |
|-------|----------|-----|
| **Single input size** | Standard bench | [Basic Usage](./criterium.basic_usage_notebook.html) |
| **Range of sizes** | Domain benchmarking | [Domain Bench](./criterium.domain_bench_notebook.html) |
| **Complexity analysis** | Domain with model fitting | [Domain Analysis](./criterium.analyse_domain_notebook.html) |
| **Automated sweeps** | Domain builder | [Domain Builder](./criterium.domain_builder_notebook.html) |

## Comparing implementations?

| Comparison Type | Approach | See |
|-----------------|----------|-----|
| **Two implementations** | Run bench on each, compare means | [Basic Usage](./criterium.basic_usage_notebook.html) |
| **Multiple implementations** | Domain with :impl axis | [Domain Bench](./criterium.domain_bench_notebook.html) |
| **Scaling comparison** | Domain analysis across sizes | [Domain Analysis](./criterium.analyse_domain_notebook.html) |

## Additional considerations

### Memory and allocations

If allocation pressure matters, enable allocation tracking:

- [Allocation Tracking](./criterium.allocation_tracking_notebook.html) - Analyze where allocations occur
- [Allocation Bench](./criterium.allocation_bench_notebook.html) - Integrated allocation analysis

### Call structure

For understanding internal behavior:

- [Call Tracing](./criterium.call_tracing_notebook.html) - Method call analysis with visualization
